name: Character AI
tagline: Chat with user-created AI personas that stay in character across long conversations.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanic here is a system prompt, a chat log, and a streaming token endpoint, which an agent can assemble before your coffee gets cold. Your own personas, your own memory file, no content filter deciding what your wizard is allowed to say: all of that is one sitting of work. What you cannot build is the browsable pile of millions of community-made characters, which is where most people actually spend their time, or the tuned model that holds a voice for hours without drifting into generic assistant-speak. You also inherit the bill: their free tier eats inference costs that you will either pay per token or pay for in GPU heat. So the private version is real and often better behaved, the discovery layer and the mobile habit are not coming with you.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define characters as editable prompt cards and hold streaming, persistent conversations with them against a local or API model.
requirements: Ollama with a decent instruct model locally, or an OpenAI-compatible API key
GPU or patience if you go local
Manual writing of each character card
whatYouLose: The character library: millions of community bots, trending lists, other people's better prompt writing
Mobile apps and push-style habit loops, you get a browser tab
Their persona-tuned model, which holds a voice longer than a generic instruct model does
Voice calls, group chats, images, and the rest of the feature drift
Free-at-the-margin inference: your version has a token bill or a fan noise problem
moatNotes: The user-generated character catalog is the actual product; the model is the runtime.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for the plus tier to skip queues and get faster responses, which is a pure infrastructure benefit you cannot self-host away without buying hardware. Beyond that, the reason anyone opens the app at all is that someone else already wrote the character: the appeal is browsing, not authoring. A private clone assumes you enjoy writing prompt cards, and most users demonstrably do not.
notes: The chat loop is a weekend afternoon; the reason you keep coming back is a catalog you did not write.
prompt:
Build a local character roleplay chat app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, single user on localhost.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/chat.db, migrations run on boot.
- Model calls go to an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint with streaming.
- Config in .env only: LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL. Default LLM_BASE_URL to http://localhost:11434/v1 so Ollama works out of the box.

Data model:
- characters: id, name, avatar_emoji, greeting, persona (long text), example_dialogue (long text), created_at.
- chats: id, character_id, title, created_at.
- messages: id, chat_id, role, content, created_at.

Features in scope:
- Character list page with create, edit, duplicate, delete. Import and export a character as a single JSON file.
- Chat page: message list, streaming assistant replies token by token, stop button, retry last reply, edit any past message in place, delete from a message onward to branch.
- Prompt assembly: system message built from persona plus example dialogue, then the last N messages that fit a configurable token budget, then a rolling summary of everything older, stored on the chat row and regenerated in the background when it falls behind.
- Per-character settings: temperature, max tokens, optional author's note injected just above the latest user turn.
- Full text search over messages.

Out of scope, do not build: auth, voice, images, group chats, mobile app, any hosted deployment, moderation filters.

Ship a README with setup in under ten lines, seed three sample characters, and make sure npm run dev works in an empty folder after npm install.
